ops.body:
**Correction to the previous comment: this task is NOT being closed.** Three of five acceptance criteria are met; two are genuinely blocked, and closing over them would misreport the state.

**Met** — consumer modules bumped and released (all 14); no `~/com.*` on either host, plus `~/.daemonkit/agents/` removed entirely and a passing plant-a-decoy negative check; every cask-installed consumer reinstalled from a tap release rather than a local build.

**Not met, both tracing to the same blocker:**

- *"Every one of the 14 LaunchAgents reloaded and running against the new state root."* On this workstation `com.yasyf.cc-pool` is **not registered at all** — I booted it out before upgrading (per the ErrUntrusted rule), and both `ccp package install` and `ccp service install` then failed. `com.yasyf.cc-pool.status.fusekit` is registered but loops at status 1 on both hosts. `com.yasyf.cc-patch.watch`/`.heal` are status 1 on both hosts on a drifted patch, unrelated to daemonkit.
- *"`ccp add` provisions an account end to end on both hosts."* Cannot even be attempted: `ccp doctor` reports `daemon status op: daemonkit: daemon is starting` and never settles.

**The blocker** is `CCPoolStatus: FuseKit runtime start failed: publish exact source fleet: catalog: tenant generation mismatch`, from `~/.cc-pool/fusekit/catalog.sqlite`. It is **not** a migration artifact — proven, not assumed: after wiping every dead daemonkit directory for cc-pool so it started from a completely clean v0.23.0 state root, it failed identically within seconds with a fresh timestamp. It reproduces on both hosts.

**Why I did not fix it here rather than routing it.** Not scope-shedding — three concrete reasons. A dedicated session (`fusekit-catalog-wedge-bug`) is actively on it and duplicating that work would race it. The fix lives in the cc-pool and fusekit trees, both of which currently hold substantial uncommitted work from concurrent sessions that I am specifically constrained not to mutate. And "recreate the tenant catalog" is a user-data decision, not a mechanical repair. What stewardship *did* mean here was giving that session evidence it did not have: the clean-state-root proof that exonerates daemonkit, the both-hosts reproduction, the distinct error strings from `holder.log`, and the observation that released `ccp` 0.68.0 has no `reset` verb — so a user who hits this has no shipped escape hatch.

**Also deliberately left undone:** `com.yasyf.cc-pool` stays unregistered on this workstation. Its plist still points at the stale staged binary `~/.daemonkit/bin/com.yasyf.cc-pool`, dated Aug 17, which is 0.66.0 on daemonkit **v0.22.0** — bootstrapping it would recreate `~/.daemonkit/agents/<label>` and resurrect the generation this task exists to remove. It should come back via `ccp package install && ccp service install` once the runtime can start, which re-stages it at 0.68.0.

**To close this task:** the catalog wedge is resolved, `com.yasyf.cc-pool` is re-registered at 0.68.0 with its state under `~/.daemonkit/a/`, and `ccp add` completes on both hosts. The cc-patch patch drift is tracked separately and should not gate this.
